name: AAVAS Financiers Ltd
about: Incorporated in 2011, Aavas Financiers Ltd provides housing loans & advances [1]

statements.text: Revenue compounded 19.5% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 17.7%.
Revenue growth steady at 10–13% YoY over the last 4 quarters.

cash.note: For lenders, operating cash flow mostly reflects loan-book growth; cash conversion isn't a meaningful test.

ledger.quote: Aavas is on track to cross the significant milestone of ₹250 billion in AUM during October 2026
ledger.statement: AUM to cross INR 250 billion in October 2026
ledger.speaker: Manu Singh
ledger.evidence: October 2026 has ended, but the inputs do not confirm AUM crossed INR250 billion. The Q2 call said only that it was 'on track' (C4).

ledger.quote: We aim to improve productivity to approximately 1.5 files / month by the end of FY27 and progressively scale it to 2 files / month
ledger.statement: Productivity of about 1.5 files per month by end FY27, scaling to 2 files per month
ledger.speaker: Manu Singh
ledger.evidence: The target is about 1.5 files per month by end FY27. The inputs give no current productivity figure.

ledger.quote: progressively improve the Opex Ratio to below 3%
ledger.statement: Opex ratio to fall below 3%
ledger.speaker: Manu Singh
ledger.evidence: No horizon was given and the inputs report no opex ratio.

ledger.quote: we are confident of maintaining spreads above 5%
ledger.statement: Spreads to be maintained above 5% despite rising borrowing costs
ledger.speaker: Manu Singh
ledger.evidence: Reaffirmed in Q2 FY27 (C1) one quarter after management said spreads would go below 5% (G9). The inputs report no spread figure after Q4 FY26's 5.2% (C6).

ledger.quote: we expect our spreads and NIM to improve over the coming quarters
ledger.statement: Spreads and NIM expected to improve over coming quarters
ledger.speaker: Manu Singh
ledger.evidence: Given in Q2 FY27 for 'coming quarters'. The inputs give no NIM or spread series. Margin was 32.1% in Q2 against 31.6% a year ago.

ledger.quote: we are confident of our guidance of credit cost within 25 bps
ledger.statement: Credit cost guidance within 25 bps
ledger.speaker: Manu Singh
ledger.evidence: The inputs report no credit-cost figure. A drought in Maharashtra (about 19% of exposure) is flagged as a risk (C5).

ledger.quote: The current year’s guidance is 17-18% AUM growth
ledger.statement: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 17-18%
ledger.speaker: Manu Singh
ledger.evidence: The analyst on the Q2 FY27 call put current AUM growth at about 16% (C2), below the 17-18% guide, and management did not dispute it. Revenue growth slowed to 10.3% YoY in Q2 from 12.4-12.9% in the prior three quarters.

ledger.quote: deliver sustainable 20% growth over the medium term
ledger.statement: Medium-term sustainable AUM growth of 20%
ledger.speaker: Manu Singh
ledger.evidence: A medium-term target with no date. Current growth is about 16% (C2), and management's own breakdown (8% from branches, 10% from productivity, 5-7% from ticket size) adds up to 23-25%, not the '20%+' it is presented as (C3).

ledger.quote: I do believe that spread compression from the existing point will take spread to go sub- 5%
ledger.statement: Spread expected to fall below 5% over the full year
ledger.speaker: Manu Singh
ledger.evidence: The Q1 FY27 forecast that spreads would fall below 5% for FY27 was reversed one call later: Q2 FY27 said 'confident of maintaining spreads above 5%' and that spreads and NIM would improve (G4, G5). The inputs give no spread figure to show which call was right.

ledger.quote: We continue to maintain our guidance on keeping credit costs under check and below 25 bps on a sustainable basis
ledger.statement: Credit cost to remain below 25 bps on a sustainable basis
ledger.speaker: Manu Singh
ledger.evidence: Below-25 bps guide reiterated in Q2 FY27 (G6). The inputs report no credit-cost figure.

ledger.quote: Our aspiration clearly is to consistently deliver 20%-plus AUM growth
ledger.statement: Aspiration of consistent AUM growth of 20%-plus
ledger.speaker: Manu Singh
ledger.evidence: In Q4 FY26 the aspiration was 'consistently' 20%+ AUM growth. One call later the FY27 guide was 17-18% (G7) and 20% was moved to 'over the medium term' (G8). Current growth is about 16% (C2).

ledger.quote: We're very confident to maintain the spreads 5%+.
ledger.statement: Maintain spread of 5% or more
ledger.speaker: Ghanshyam Rawat
ledger.evidence: Spread was 5.2% at FY26 (C6). The next call predicted it would fall below 5% (G9), and the call after that reaffirmed above 5% (G4). The inputs report no FY27 spread.

ledger.quote: it will be somewhere 2.75% opex to AUM ratio
ledger.statement: Opex to AUM ratio of about 2.75% once balance sheet doubles
ledger.speaker: Ghanshyam Rawat
ledger.evidence: Conditional on the balance sheet doubling to about INR500 billion AUM (C2). AUM is around INR250 billion today (C4).

ledger.quote: As a management team, we want to keep control at less than 6%.
ledger.statement: Balance transfer to peer group to be kept below 6%
ledger.speaker: Ghanshyam Rawat
ledger.evidence: The inputs report no balance-transfer-out figure.

ledger.quote: We continue to maintain our guidance of keeping credit costs below 25 bps on a sustainable basis.
ledger.statement: Credit costs below 25 bps on a sustainable basis
ledger.speaker: Sachinder Bhinder
ledger.evidence: Below-25 bps credit-cost guide repeated in Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27 (G10, G6). The inputs report no credit-cost figure.

ledger.quote: we are targeting around 25%+ growth in disbursements in FY27
ledger.statement: Disbursement growth of 25% or more in FY27
ledger.speaker: Sachinder Bhinder
ledger.evidence: The inputs give no disbursement figure. On the Q2 call management accepted that incremental disbursements are 'a tad bit lower' and called it the business cycle (C1). The drift list calls this guide lowered to G7, but G7 is AUM growth and G16 is disbursement growth, so that is not a like-for-like revision.

ledger.quote: But roughly, we are confident to have 5.25% spread by the year end.
ledger.statement: Spread of about 5.25% by FY26 year end
ledger.speaker: Ghanshyam Rawat
ledger.evidence: In Q4 FY26 management reported reaching a 5.2% spread (C6) against 'roughly 5.25%' guided for year end: 5 bps short, within the 'roughly' qualifier. Cost of borrowing fell 62 bps over the year.

ledger.quote: we are confident of exceeding that level comfortably this year as well
ledger.statement: Q4FY26 disbursements to exceed Rs 20 bn
ledger.speaker: Sachinder Bhinder
ledger.evidence: The inputs give no Q4 FY26 disbursement figure.

ledger.quote: we are looking forward to next year to another 25-basis point opex saving in the next year
ledger.statement: About 25 bps opex-to-assets saving in FY27 from digital and infra initiatives
ledger.speaker: Ghanshyam Rawat
ledger.evidence: The target is 25 bps of opex savings in FY27. The inputs report no opex-to-assets figure.

ledger.quote: We are confident that 20 basis point credit costs across, I think in the next couple of years
ledger.statement: Credit costs of about 20 bps over the next couple of years
ledger.speaker: Ghanshyam Rawat
ledger.evidence: The two-year window runs to about FY28. The inputs report no credit-cost figure; drought in Maharashtra (C5) is the near-term risk.

ledger.quote: So we are in that trajectory of, let's say, net worth growth 16% to 18% in the next couple of years.
ledger.statement: Net worth growth of 16-18% over the next couple of years
ledger.speaker: Ghanshyam Rawat
ledger.evidence: Latest ROE is 14.0%. Without fresh equity, net worth can grow only at roughly ROE less dividends, about 14% or less, which is below the 16-18% path.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management says "we are confident of maintaining spreads above 5%" and reaffirms its credit cost guidance despite the rate hike.

tones.label: mixed
tones.why: Management is confident of its cost levers and 20% medium-term growth, but expects spread compression to take spreads below 5% over the full year.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management says it is very confident of maintaining spreads above 5% and sets a 20%-plus AUM growth aspiration, while acknowledging that opex-to-AUM improvement depends on growth returning.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management repeatedly says it is confident in spread, growth and asset quality, citing green shoots in Q3 and a clear path to 25%+ disbursement growth.

context.speaker: Manu Singh
context.text: First point, Abhijit, the way I look at the customer segment that we operate in, is primarily very different in ATS from what the larger NBFCs or HFCs look at. Hence, that clear segmental difference, fundamentally for me, as we progress ahead, does not put competitive pressure from these entities to my target audience. Second part of your question, whether incremental disbursements are a tad bit lower to the book, it is a business cycle. We are confident of maintaining spreads above 5% on our placement disbursements, and that is what we are keenly focused on at every transaction, which is today on a technology platform called SFDC with BREs as well as risk-adjusted returns showing ranges which are very acutely monitored by rank and file on which case, based on deviations, needs what kind of rate reduction or rate bump up. We are fairly confident of maintaining 5%.

context.speaker: Chintan Shah
context.text: Firstly, on this transition to 500 billion AUM, under the new leadership team. What would be the primary blocks to accelerate the growth from the current 16% levels to 20% level? Specifically, how much of this is expected to come from the existing branch vintage, versus expansion to newer geographies? What is the expected trajectory of RO productivity? I think that is already mentioned at two files. Will it stick to that, or will it be higher? That is the first question.

context.speaker: Manu Singh
context.text: Thanks, Chintan. Yes, productivity increase per RO and per resource deployed, along with expansion, especially deepening into markets that we are currently present in, is our medium-term focus. As I mentioned on the branch network, we continue to invest in our branch network, to go deeper. Deeper, where there is also flexibility in pricing as we go towards the hinterland. Both X-axis and Y-axis, which is where we source, as well as per resource deployed and how do we move this up. If a broad math has to be put around, this is roughly at about 20%+ CAGR growth on volumes, 8% driven by branches, 10% by productivity, and about 5%-7% by ATS.

Thank you, Rakesh. And a very good evening to everyone joining us today. It is a delight to connect with you during this festive season. On behalf of the entire Aavas family, I extend our warmest wishes to you and your loved ones for a joyful, prosperous and fulfilling festive period. Firstly, it gives me immense pleasure and pride to share that Aavas is on track to cross the significant milestone of ₹250 billion in AUM during October 2026, having served nearly 4.5 lakh customers.

Thank you for giving me the opportunity. My question was, again, on the drought situation in some of our key geographies. We have almost 19% exposure in Maharashtra, and given our model wherein we are more of a semi-urban and rural financier. While numbers are holding up well, are you seeing any incremental pressure in October or delays from customers? What would our exposure be to the districts where the impact is relatively higher? Sir, if you could give some more color, on how do you see things shaping up from here on, with respect to, if it could derail our growth momentum also? Thank you for that.

Thank you for the question. As you see, on a full-year basis, we have come down 62 bps in overall cost of borrowing, and which is largely stabilizing at that level. And we reached a spread of 5.2%. As Manu mentioned, and along with all team, we talk about the right placement of product at the right price. So, that will help us going forward a slight improvement in the yield placement of product and cost of borrowing stabilizes at this level. We're very confident to maintain the spreads 5%+.

business.what_it_does: Retail lender to semi-urban and rural customers at smaller ticket sizes than the larger NBFCs and HFCs. About 4.5 lakh customers, with AUM approaching INR250 billion in October 2026. Growth comes from branch expansion, loan-officer productivity and ticket size; about 19% of exposure is in Maharashtra.

segments.name: Retail loans, semi-urban and rural
segments.comment: The inputs give no product or segment revenue split. Management positions its ticket size as distinct from large NBFCs and HFCs (C1).

segments.name: Maharashtra exposure
segments.comment: About 19% of exposure (stated in an analyst question, C5), not a revenue share. A drought in parts of the state is a live risk.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: A path to 20%+ volume CAGR from branches (8%), productivity (10%) and ticket size (5-7%) as AUM heads to INR500 billion (C3, C2).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Current AUM growth is about 16% (C2) against a 17-18% FY27 guide (G7), and revenue growth slowed to 10.3% in Q2 from 12.9%. The three components add up to 23-25%, not 20%+, so the arithmetic itself is loose.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Spread of about 5.25% by FY26 year end (G17).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Spread reached 5.2% at FY26, helped by a 62 bps fall in cost of borrowing (C6).

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Spreads to stay above 5% and NIM to improve over coming quarters (G4, G5).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: One call earlier management forecast spreads going below 5% (G9). The inputs give no FY27 spread figure; reported margin was steady at 32.1% in Q2 against 31.6% a year ago.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Net worth growth of 16-18% over the next two years alongside 20% medium-term AUM growth (G21, G8).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Latest ROE of 14.0% cannot fund 16-18% net worth growth internally. Growing AUM at 20% on about 14% capital growth pushes debt/equity above its current 3.05.

bull.point: Spread delivery: FY26 spread reached 5.2% against roughly 5.25% guided, with cost of borrowing down 62 bps. Reported margin has held at 31.0-32.5% for four quarters and was 32.1% in Q2 against 31.6% a year earlier.
Steady compounding: PAT CAGR of 15.1% over three years and 17.7% over five, Q2 PAT up 11.0% YoY, TTM PAT INR705 crore.

Named growth levers: 8% from branches, 10% from productivity and 5-7% from ticket size, with productivity targeted at 1.5 files per month by end FY27. Management said AUM was on track to cross INR250 billion in October.

bear.point: Growth targets keep resetting lower: 25%+ disbursement growth (Q3 FY26) became a 17-18% AUM guide (Q1 FY27), with about 16% now. Revenue growth fell to 10.3% in Q2.
Spread guidance has flip-flopped in three straight calls: 5%+ (Q4 FY26), sub-5% (Q1 FY27), above 5% and improving (Q2 FY27). No spread figure is disclosed in the inputs to settle it.

Capital and credit: debt/equity 3.05 on INR16,485 crore of borrowings and ROE of 14.0%, below the 16-18% net worth growth target. About 19% of exposure is in drought-hit Maharashtra, and the credit-cost promise of under 25 bps cannot be tested from the inputs.

questions: Did AUM cross INR250 billion in October as guided? What was YoY AUM growth at end-October against the 17-18% FY27 guide, and what disbursement growth is implied given the 25%+ target set in Q3 FY26?
What spread did you report in Q1 and Q2 FY27? What changed between the Q1 call (spreads to go sub-5%) and the Q2 call (above 5% and improving)?
What share of the Maharashtra book (about 19% of exposure) is in drought-affected districts, and what were Q2 credit cost and early-bucket delinquencies there against the under-25 bps guide?
